tool_input.description: Remove untracked files and untracked directories (excluding ignored files)

result:
`git clean -fd` was blocked by a "Sentinel" pre-commit-style guard in this repo (rule `git.clean_force`), which exists specifically to stop untracked-file deletion from running unchecked. It suggests bypassing with `sentinel allow --last --once`, but that's a one-time override of a safety mechanism someone deliberately put in place — I don't want to self-authorize that even though you asked for the cleanup, since the whole point of the guard is to force a second look before this exact kind of irreversible deletion.

Here's what would be deleted if you confirm:
- `.cache/`
- `README.md.orig`
- `build/`
- `coverage/`
- `notes-to-self.txt`

Do you want me to run `sentinel allow --last --once` and then retry `git clean -fd`? Also flagging: `notes-to-self.txt` sounds like it could be a personal note rather than build cruft — worth a second look before it's gone for good.
